summary: 60-minute style console walkthrough focused on per-route dashboards and cost decomposition. Customer is evaluating Redwood for inference hosting: primary concerns are token cost, latency SLOs for real-time chat, and data residency/VPC. Team requested concrete batching/quantization suggestions and a short POC to validate latency under Alkira traffic patterns.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Samir from Redwood, AE for the Alkira account. We'll do a quick agenda: console walkthrough, per-route telemetry, cost breakdown, then Q&A and next steps. Lena will demo the console.
[00:23] Jordan (Alkira): Hey thanks. Quick note — we have about 150k monthly active users hitting chat flows, most traffic is short chat (avg 40 tokens out) but occasional long assist flows. Our SLO target is p95 < 300ms for short requests.\n[00:40] Maya (Alkira): And platform question: we'll need VPC + KMS; also SOC 2 is table stakes. How does Redwood handle key management and audit logs?
[00:55] Lena (Redwood SE): Good q. We support customer KMS integration for private, we also ship audit logs to your S3 or SIEM, and SSO via SAML. We can show the audit tab later.
[01:12] Diego (Redwood): For the cost side we want to show per-route cost slices; you can see token breakdown and infra allocation.
[01:25] Jordan: Awesome, curious on per-route attribution — we have a couple of models in play and want to stop surprises on the bill.
[01:40] Lena: Ok jumping into the console — loading Routes dashboard. Note: this is a sandbox view with anonymized names. Top left you see overall throughput, p50/p95 latency, and cost per 1k requests.
[02:05] Lena: Here is the route table — each route maps to a front-end intent. You can pin a model variant (ex: gpt-neox-30b-q4) or Redwood-managed open model.
[02:25] Jordan: Wait, does Redwood do automatic fallback if a model is unavailable or overloaded?
[02:33] Samir: Yes, routing policies can do region fallback or model variant fallback. We can do a canary or weighted rollout too.
[02:45] Maya: For PII data, we need request-level redaction, are there hooks?
[02:50] Lena: We offer request-level masking and you can use our private deployment to keep traffic inside VPC. Also you can store KV-cache local to your cluster. Sometimes the transcription says "KV cash" but it's KV cache, so watch for that.
[03:10] Diego: Now cost decomposition — pull up the cost lens for route "patient-assist". You can see tokens broken into prompt vs completion, infra cost per GPU-hour, caching savings, and Optimize suggestions.
[03:35] Lena: Note the Optimize tile — it suggests enabling prefix caching for that route and reducing batch size for short chats to keep latency tight; it also recommends a quantized model for background summarization routes.
[03:52] Jordan: How confident are those suggestions? Are they heuristics or from benchmarking?
[03:58] Lena: We run workload-aware heuristics combined with sampling runs on your payloads in the sandbox; Optimize also simulates per-token unit economics. For the patient-assist route we estimate a 27% token cost reduction with prefix caching enabled.
[04:20] Maya: Show the per-token dashboards — I want to understand how we get from tokens to dollars.
[04:25] Lena: Right — token counters are grouped by tokenizer; you can see token inflation on templates, and suggested prompt truncation. In the cost tab we map tokens to GPU time using our kernel-selector model which estimates throughput by seq length.
[04:45] Jordan: What about batching? Our traffic is spiky, 200 reqs/sec in bursts — will bigger batch sizes hurt latency?
[04:52] Diego: Good point — Redwood allows continuous batching with tail latency awareness. For short chat we recommend small max_batch=8 with adaptive timeout 10ms, that keeps p95 low while still gaining some batching efficiency.
[05:15] Lena: I'll show the live simulator — running a synthetic short-chat workload. You can slide the burst slider.
[05:30] [simulation noises]
[05:33] Lena: See p95 creeps to 320ms when batch hits 32, but with max_batch=8 we stay under 260ms. The console flags SLO violations and shows cost delta.
[05:50] Jordan: That helps. For cost numbers, are infra costs shown per route or rolled up?
[05:55] Lena: Both — routes have their own infra tag and we can attribute GPU hours and memory. We also show amortized storage for KV cache and network costs for VPC egress if any.
[06:12] Maya: On the security side, can we audit who changed a route config? We need that for compliance.
[06:18] Lena: Yes audit logs include user, IP, change diff, and we can push to your SIEM.
[06:25] Jordan: Any mention of encryption in transit at the route level?
[06:29] Samir: TLS in transit and KMS for at-rest keys; for private deployments we can also integrate HSM.
[06:40] Lena: Back to Optimize — here's a sample recommendation: quantize model X to int8 for the background summarizer route. It shows expected latency increase/decrease and cost savings.
[06:58] Jordan: Is there any loss in output quality with quantization? Our summaries are clinical — we can't degrade accuracy too much.
[07:05] Lena: Optimize attaches a QA delta estimate based on evals against your prompt set. For clinical summarization it flagged a small ROUGE drop for int8 on that specific model; suggestion was int8 only for non-critical routes.
[07:25] Maya: Could we do mixed deployment — hosted for public-facing chat and private for PHI routes?
[07:30] Samir: Absolutely — many customers do hybrid: hosted for scale, dedicated or private for PHI. Routing rules can select based on tag or header.
[07:45] Jordan: Let's talk about pricing — how do you charge for dedicated vs hosted for high throughput?
[07:52] Samir: Hosted is usage-based (per-token + infra markup). Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commitment; you pay for reserved GPU-hours and get predictable latency and cost per token. We'll share a pricing sheet after the call.
[08:12] Diego: Also note burst credits — dedicated customers get a small on-demand burst pool for sudden spikes.
[08:30] Lena: Now I want to show route-level anomaly detection — console flagged a 3x spike in tokenization for route "intake-form" two days ago and traced it to a template change.
[08:50] Jordan: That's useful — we often see template drift. Does Redwood integrate with our CI to automatically run token inflation checks on template commits?
[08:58] Samir: Yes, webhook integration can run quick preflight checks and warn on token growth.
[09:12] Maya: If we run a POC, what telemetry do you need from us?
[09:18] Lena: Ideally sample payloads, expected traffic shape, and SLOs. We can ingest logs (anonymized) into the sandbox to run more accurate Optimize sims.
[09:32] Jordan: Can we try a quick check of KV cache hit rate impact?
[09:36] Lena: Yes — we can run a 48-hour experiment in the sandbox and show savings. That usually surfaces for templated prompts with repeat prefixes.
[09:50] Diego: On the console you'll see cache hit % by route, and the cost delta if you enable KV cache.
[10:05] Lena: Demoing the Billing tab — you can pivot by model, route, or tag; we also export per-hour CSV for your invoicing.
[10:25] Jordan: Do you show forecasted spend if we change batch settings?
[10:30] Lena: Yep — the simulation lets you toggle batch size, enable caching, change model quantization and it updates forecast.
[10:40] Maya: Anything on data residency? We need EU residency for some patients.
[10:45] Samir: We have region pinning and can constrain routes to EU-only regions; private deployments let you host entirely on-prem if needed.
[11:00] Jordan: Competitors sometimes hide their kernel assumptions — how transparent are your throughput estimates?
[11:06] Diego: We publish model performance profiles and kernel footprints per GPU type. The console shows the kernel selector's chosen kernel and expected tokens/sec.
[11:25] Lena: small hiccup, my screen share stuttered — sorry.
[11:30] Jordan: No worries. Can we also look at long-tail latencies? A lot of our users care about 99th percentile for certain flows.
[11:38] Lena: The route view has p50/p95/p99 charts and you can filter by seq length. P99 can be used to set autoscale triggers.
[11:55] Maya: On scale, how does autoscaling interact with sustained bursts?
[11:59] Diego: Autoscaling uses a smoothing window and reserve capacity for spikes; dedicated customers can configure min instances and a burst policy.
[12:14] Jordan: For private deployments, what's involved for the infra team — roughly how long to stand up?
[12:20] Samir: Typical private deployment (VPC-managed) takes 4-6 weeks with customer infra support; on-prem longer depending on network and HSM.
[12:35] Maya: Do you support container registries and custom images?
[12:40] Lena: Yes, we can run models from your container registry in private, though we validate images for safety.
[12:55] Jordan: Any examples from other health customers?
[13:00] Samir: We have a reference architecture and anonymized case study; I'll share the deck. One customer saved ~30% tokens after adopting prefix caching and route split for background tasks.
[13:15] Lena: Switching to Route comparison — you can select multiple routes and compare cost per 1k, p95, and cache hit.
[13:32] Jordan: Can we do per-team chargeback?
[13:36] Lena: Yes tagging and billing exports let you map routes to teams and allocate costs. You can set quotas per team as well.
[13:50] Maya: How fine-grained are the RBAC controls? We need least privilege for infra and product teams.
[13:55] Samir: RBAC supports role templates, custom roles, and token-scoped permissions. We also support SCIM for group sync.
[14:10] Jordan: Ok can we review the POC success criteria? We want to validate: 1) p95 < 300ms on short chat under 200 req/s bursts, 2) cost per 1k requests < $X (TBD), 3) KV cache hit >= 40% for templated flows.
[14:30] Samir: Noted — we'll draft SLI/SLO doc and include those metrics.
[14:40] Lena: Now quick look at canary rollouts — you can route 5% traffic to new model and monitor quality regression via eval hooks.
[15:00] Jordan: Eval hooks — can you run our prompt set automatically post-deploy?
[15:06] Lena: Yes, we can schedule evals and tie regression alerts to rollout policies.
[15:20] Maya: For the billing CSV, does it include per-token breakdown per request id?
[15:25] Diego: We provide per-request token counts in detailed exports but roll them up for invoices; exports can be matched to your request IDs.
[15:40] Jordan: Let's talk about latency vs cost tradeoffs concretely for our two main routes: short-chat (low tokens) and long-summarize (high tokens).
[15:50] Lena: Short-chat: small batch, low timeout, maybe cheaper smaller model; long-summarize: use larger batch and quantized model or a cheaper open model. We'll put numbers in the playbook.
[16:10] Maya: Any hidden costs — e.g., Kafka or egress when using VPC?
[16:15] Samir: We'll call out egress and network costs in the cost model, they show up separate from compute in the console.
[16:25] Jordan: How do we validate model parity between hosted and private? We'll need exact same weights and behavior.
[16:32] Lena: For private we run the same model artifacts; we can do A/B tests and hash checks. Some tokenization differences can exist if tokenizer versions vary; we standardize tokenizer in the artifact bundle.
[16:50] Maya: Can the console store anonymized transcripts for debugging? We have strict PHI rules.
[16:56] Samir: We can store anonymized or opt-out of storage; for PHI you can choose to not persist completions and stream them to your controlled logs.
[17:10] Jordan: Ok let's cover the POC logistics — what telemetry do you need, and who on our side should be involved?
[17:18] Samir: We'll need a platform engineer (Maya), ML owner (Jordan), and someone from security (Carlos) to sign off on private networking. We'll coordinate on data sharing and sandbox credentials.
[17:35] Maya: One last infra Q — do you support multi-AZ for high availability?
[17:40] Diego: Yes multi-AZ is supported in hosted and dedicated; private depends on your infra but we can recommend patterns.
[17:52] Lena: Wrapping up: I'll send the console screenshots and a sample CSV export. Also sending an Optimize config sample that auto-suggests caching and quantization for routes.
[18:05] Jordan: Great. A couple small clarifications later via email is fine.
[18:10] Samir: Recap — next steps and action items: Samir sends pricing & deck, Lena shares playbook and telemetry export, Alkira team runs synthetic test and provides traffic samples. Any blockers?
[18:25] Maya: No blockers; timeline wise we want a POC next week if possible.
[18:30] Samir: We'll propose 2026-05-12 for POC kickoff. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and materials.
[18:40] Jordan: Thanks, bye.
[18:42] [call ended]

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription mixed some speaker labels and misheard technical terms (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache", "kernel selector" sometimes transcribed as "kernel sector"). The console demo included several screen-shares; portions where Lena is describing charts are summarized verbatim but exact numeric tables attached in follow-up materials.
